body.statement: For every prespecified \(\delta\in[0,1]\), the projection of \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) onto the latent type-mass vector is exactly \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). Every compatible full law induces one \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\), and every \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) lifts to a law in \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) reproducing \(b\), \(q\), \(\pi\), the history-indexed controlled responses, and the priming-fraction restriction.
body.justification: Projection equality prevents a reduced optimizer under a disclosed priming sensitivity value from being mistaken for an unattainable collection of armwise or periodwise marginals.
body.gap: Balke and Pearl (1997) establish the response-type template, while Janvin and Stensrud (2025) construct single-pathogen endpoint laws; neither gives this two-period variant-history projection with external margins and bounded noninfecting-exposure priming.
body.consumer: Investigators combining vaccine trials with variant-surveillance panels obtain a finite feasibility test and full-law certificate for every reported bound.
